To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
child maltreatment victims who develop resilience are those who are able to use their personal characteristics and life circumstances to cope with their maltreatment.
child abuse and neglect victims who do well have certain personal and environmental protective factors that ameliorate the negative emotional sequelae of maltreatment.

child maltreatment survivors are more likely to be resilient when they (1) have access to good health care, educational, and other social services; (2) develop personal characteristics that help them survive; (3) are able to form and utilize relationships for survival; and (4) experience abuse-specific protective factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the factors that promote resilience in child maltreatment survivors.
the factors that foster resilience in child maltreatment survivors.
the factors that contribute to the resilience of children exposed to maltreatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
resilience in maltreated children is a function of the interaction of the child's personal characteristics and skills with the protective factors of the environment.

the child who is resilient is one whose environment provides the necessary protective factors for survival, and who has personal characteristics or skills that foster the development and utilization of these protective factors.
resilience in child victims of maltreatment is a complex phenomenon that is affected by a number of interacting personal characteristics and environmental factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the development of resilience is fostered when children are able to develop a sense of control over their lives, have a sense of belonging to a safe and supportive community, and have a sense of purpose in life.
children's resilience is a function of both personal characteristics and life circumstances, with the latter being more important than the former in determining long-term outcome.
resilience is a relative concept and is fostered by both personal and environmental protective factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resilience can be enhanced through the development and use of effective interventions that address both personal protective factors and the environment.
child maltreatment is not always a life sentence of misery and dysfunction.
the resilience of child maltreatment victims is a function of both personal characteristics and the life circumstances of the child, and both need to be addressed in treatment.
